description: Split a PDF into several new PDFs, one per range. Page numbers start at 1 (the check tools return 0-based `page` values: add 1). Each range is a page spec (numbers and ranges) of consecutive pages in order, such as ["1-3"] or [4,5]; each file is named `<prefix>-p<first>-<last>.pdf` (or `<prefix>-p<first>.pdf` for one page) inside `outputDir`. All files are created or none are. Writes a NEW .pdf inside the allowed folder and never changes or overwrites an existing file. Layers and static XFA are dropped (listed in `lost`); digital signatures are removed. Example: {"pdfPath":"book.pdf","ranges":[["1-10"],["11-20"]],"outputDir":"parts","prefix":"book"}. This is not redaction and does not sanitise: pages you leave out are not copied, but document metadata, bookmark titles and anything a kept page shares with an omitted page can remain. Use redact_pdf to remove sensitive content. Nothing is uploaded.

outputDir.description: existing folder inside the allowed folder (the allowed folder itself is fine)

pdfPath.description: path to the PDF, inside the allowed folder

prefix.description: file name prefix: letters, digits, . _ -, up to 64

ranges.description: one page spec per output file

items.description: A page number like 3 or a range like "2-5". A bare-number string ("5"), a leading zero, a reversed range and a repeated page are refused.

name: split_pdf
title: Split PDF
